_format.purpose: Ground truth for the Slice 9b precision harness (crates/nerve-index/tests/py_precision.rs). Written before py-reference existed, as fixtures/ts-resolution/expected.json and fixtures/py-basic/expected.json were. See README.md.
_format.selector: <rel_path>#<qualified_name>, where qualified_name is scope_path.name (or just name at module top level). <rel_path> on its own names that file's Module entity.
_format.resolved: Every AST_RESOLVED CALLS/REFERENCES/EXTENDS edge the corpus must contain, and the only ones it may contain. A missing one is a false negative and fails the gate; an extra one is a false positive and fails the gate.
_format.unresolved: Every edge to an Unresolved entity, and the only ones there may be. target_name is the Unresolved entity's name; reason is py-reference's recorded reason.
_format.forbidden: Edges that must not exist in any form, resolved or unresolved. Each is the plausible wrong answer for a negative fixture.
_format.known_false_negatives: Edges a semantically complete resolver would produce and Nerve deliberately does not. Each must be ABSENT: observing one means the refusal was lifted and the entry belongs in `resolved` instead. These are what the FN column of the printed table counts, so the number is measured rather than asserted to be zero.
_format.unmodelled_call_sites: Call and base-class shapes whose form is not modelled. Counted, never guessed.
_format.no_implements: There is no IMPLEMENTS section and there never will be. Python has no `implements` keyword; `class Abstract(ABC)` states inheritance, and EXTENDS is what the syntax states.

resolved.note: same-module call
relative from-import, called inside a method
the class name in value position inside one of its own methods
explicit class receiver; the class declares the method
module-level call site; the source is the Module entity
from pkg.util import scale
import pkg.util binds pkg; pkg.util is the longest indexed prefix
import pkg.core as core
pkg/__init__.py binds Engine from .core, so pkg.Engine is pkg.core.Engine
a class body is not an enclosing scope for its methods, so the module function wins
a comprehension body reaches outward for names it does not bind
`global target` keeps the name module-scoped despite the assignment below it
a nested def is a binding in the enclosing function scope
`nonlocal helper` binds the enclosing function's name despite the assignment below it
the base is computed, but the call that computes it is real
module-level value-position reference
return annotation
parameter and return annotation
the annotation is a reference; it is not a licence to resolve the call
value-position reference inside a method
a class returned by value
the head of a subscripted base is still referenced, even though the base is not modelled
local base
base named through a module alias
imported base

forbidden.why: a local of the same name shadows the import
Python binds a name for the whole function body, not from the assignment onwards
an annotation is not a type inference licence
a same-named attribute on a different class
in the class body itself the class attribute shadows the module function
the comprehension variable shadows the module function inside the comprehension
a computed base is not the class the computing function happens to return
a subscripted base is a runtime call, not an erased type argument to be stripped

known_false_negatives.why: what `from pkg.util import *` binds lives in the imported module's runtime namespace. Slice 9a records the binding set as unknowable, and 9b does not contradict it.
`self` is a parameter name, not a language keyword. Reading it as the enclosing class would be type inference by convention, and a subclass instance is what is usually passed.
`Turbo.start` is inherited. Walking the MRO to find the declaration stops being a syntax fact as soon as one base is unresolved.
